commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Leave large shell output to the model or the harness (#10184)

This reverts the spill mode added in #10144. With
`TaskSessionSpec.tool_output_spill_bytes` set, the engine kept each
command's full stdout and stderr in the task machine and returned a
preview with the file path, so a command with unbounded output cost the
model nothing.

That cost is the signal that teaches a model to manage output, by
redirecting long output to a file and reading it with `tail` or `grep`.
A model trained with the engine catching its output loses information in
harnesses that only truncate, which is what most evaluation harnesses
do. Keeping the rest of a stream is therefore the model's job in a
training environment, and a harness that runs agents for their results
can add its own safety net. The review of #10144 also asked to move the
mechanism out of TaskCompendium's bash wrapper into the machine
backends; removing it makes that unnecessary.

Observations keep the 1 MiB truncation and the `stdout_truncated` and
`stderr_truncated` flags, and the docs now state the limit and the
policy. `TaskSessionSpec` drops `tool_output_spill_bytes`, which nothing
in this repository set to a value other than `None`; external callers
such as MarinSkyRL must drop the field when they take this release.

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <ravwojdyla@gmail.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[marina] Add a persistent Python playground (#10178)

Add a Python playground applet with a searchable project index, file
editing and uploads, package requirements, and Markdown/image previews
of generated outputs. Trusted programs run under CPython with a
120-second timeout, sharing Marina's service privileges and network
access.

Persist sources, binary inputs and the latest run using relational
Postgres tables and BYTEA blobs. Limit source and input files together
to 5 MiB and outputs to 10 MiB per project, with no quota across
projects. Replace old output blobs on reruns and reclaim all project
blobs on deletion.

Expose project operations through Marina MCP and accept ZIP imports,
with a CLI that uploads a directory using shared Marin authentication.

Make Marina's installed rigging, PyArrow and FineStore packages
available to programs while resolving extra requirements with uv.
Include a storage preview example that uses inherited object-store
credentials and Marin's bucket routing to read a bounded Parquet preview
without copying secrets into project data.

Add a hideable Loom conversation pane using Marina’s configured Loom
origin and existing read-only agent profile. Scope chat history and
drafts to each project and include its identifiers and saved revisions
in page context. Keep the playground usable when Loom is unconfigured or
unreachable.

Permit credentialed Loom browser connections from Marina's private
applet origin alongside its main origin. Keep the public applet origin
excluded and retain Loom's normal user authentication and profile
permissions.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[task-curation] Embed tasks and map curriculum coverage in Atlas (#10157)

Make task curation the canonical embedding path for tasks and curriculum
entries. Embed public instructions, answer-format requirements and tool
schemas directly with the same pinned Harrier model and retrieval rubric
used for curriculum anchors. CPU inference caches vectors and writes
Zephyr Parquet. Exact alignment loads the curriculum matrix once per
shard and streams task vectors; curriculum edits reuse task embeddings.
Publication references the scored assignment files directly. Remove the
OpenAI/SQLite curriculum experiment.

Export precomputed coverage and bounded examples through Zephyr.
Postgres receives curriculum entries, counts, and independent samples of
up to 100 tasks per source and 10 per curriculum node. The Atlas has By
source and By curriculum tabs, a map of all domains and topics, skills,
filters and sampled task details. Area navigation loads examples
automatically and interleaves datasets across pages. Full task, vector
and assignment files remain in object storage.

Converted release `1400a3d7ddfd` contains 4,998,910 task instances from
146 sources, including 1,659 evaluation instances. Its serving export is
33.8 MB of Parquet with 6,219 statistics rows and 17,875 sampled tasks.
Direct import from CW took 33 seconds; the browser became ready in under
one second. The curriculum has 45 domains, 2,450 hierarchy nodes and
5,526 embedded anchors. Fixed maximum cosine distances are 0.45 for
subjects and 0.25 for capabilities. Matches outside a cutoff remain
unassigned at that level. Assignments are approximate: narrative topics
can distract from the skill a task requires. Failed imports leave the
previously active Atlas release in place.

Default remote artifacts to `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin`, with
explicit root and local-cache overrides. The [curation
reference](docs/references/task-curation.md#pipeline-overview) diagrams
the complete graph and links its stages and data models. The [Atlas
reference](docs/references/rl-data-atlas.md) covers the serving export
and local import. The checked-in app supports review without deploying a
live Marina revision.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Carry the conversation and timing in rollout events (#10177)

Rollout events reported timing and counts but not what was said, so an
observer could not follow a long agentic attempt before `run()`
returned, and a crash lost the transcript with the record. Events also
carried uneven detail: grading and the whole attempt had no duration, an
interrupted attempt did not say why, and tool calls could not be matched
to the model's calls.

The engine's events now carry the conversation. `SessionPrepared` has
the first request's `messages` and `options`, including the advertised
tools. `ModelTurnCompleted` has the assistant `message` and the reported
`usage`. `TransitionCompleted` has the `observations` the session
returned, or the new conversation in `reset_conversation`, which it
reports even when a turn or token limit makes the engine skip the reset.
An observer can therefore rebuild the transcript for any session,
including `AgentTaskSession` and external sessions that emit no tool
events. The fields reference the attempt's own messages, so the queue
copies nothing.

`ToolCallCompleted` stays per-call detail and gains `call_id` and
`done`; its observation is the `TransitionCompleted` message with the
same `tool_call_id`. `Graded` gains the grade's `error`, `failure` and
the `duration` of output capture plus grading. `AttemptEnded` gains the
interruption's `error` and the `duration` of the whole attempt.
`SessionPrepared.message_count` and
`TransitionCompleted.observation_count` are replaced by the content they
counted.

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <ravwojdyla@gmail.com>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[eval] Run each evaluation as a StepSpec (#9813)

Run each evaluation as a StepSpec with its own lock, success cache, and
result record. Evaluations in one launch share a candidate server and
optional hosted judge. Cached evaluations are skipped on restart; a
fully cached launch starts no servers. A group StepSpec locks the launch
before starting inference so duplicate orchestrators cannot provision
duplicate servers.

Evaluators run sequentially by default. `--max-concurrent` allows
concurrent evaluators on shared inference, but omits per-evaluation
server metrics because server-wide counters include sibling traffic.
Server startup failures write infrastructure-failure records for all
pending evaluations.

Pipeline retries derive run IDs from the pipeline artifact path and
resolved model, evaluator, runtime, judge, and policy settings,
preserving completed evaluations across orchestrator resubmissions. CLI
launches and mutable pipeline versions (`dev` or `*-dev`) create fresh
runs. Verified policies retain their pinned benchmark sources and
Harbor/Evalchemy commits.

EvalDash withholds scores until each evaluation's StepSpec succeeds.
Historical records without step status keep their existing display. A
crash after writing a record but before StepRunner marks success can
rerun that evaluation. The success cache prevents completed steps from
being overwritten on ordinary restarts, addressing the failure in the
[October 6 incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/627).

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Spill large shell output to a file in the task machine (#10144)

A shell observation keeps at most the machine output limit of each
stream and drops the rest, so the model cannot see the end of a long
build log or test run.

TaskSessionSpec.tool_output_spill_bytes enables a spill mode. Each shell
command writes stdout and stderr to files under /tmp/tool-output/ in the
task machine, and the host reads only the first tool_output_spill_bytes
bytes plus one. A stream over the limit keeps its file, and the
observation returns the preview with a new stdout_path or stderr_path
field, so the model can read the rest with later commands. Shorter
streams appear in full and their files are removed. A timed-out command
reports both paths, because its files can hold output the machine did
not return.

Each saved file keeps at most the first 64 MiB of its stream
(`SPILL_FILE_BYTES`). The rest passes through a pipeline that reads and
discards it, so a command that prints without end keeps running and
cannot fill the machine's storage; up to two such files per spilled call
stay until the attempt ends.

The field is required like the other session limits; `None` turns
spilling off and keeps observations unchanged. Every `TaskSessionSpec`
construction must now pass it: in this repository that is only
`rolloutengine.test_support`, and external callers such as the SkyRL
integration must add it. Only the shell tool spills; provider tools run
on the host and return their observations in full.

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <ravwojdyla@gmail.com>

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Cap the tokens one rollout attempt spends (#10143)

An attempt was bounded only by turns and deadlines, so nothing capped
model spend. `TaskSessionSpec.max_total_tokens` now sets a per-attempt
budget, and callers must state it like the other limits: `None` means no
budget. Each model request charges `ModelTurn.request_tokens`: the
counts in the new optional `ModelTurn.usage` when the transport reports
them, as a chat endpoint can, otherwise the lengths of the turn's token
IDs. A request charges its full prompt, including the served prefix,
because a budget measures spend per request.

Without a conversation reset, the next prompt holds at least the
previous request's prompt and response. After each response the engine
therefore stops when the tokens spent plus that request's count reach
the budget, so it never sends a request whose prompt alone would reach
it; the last request sent may exceed the budget by its new observation
and response tokens. The session handles the last response, and the
engine grades the conversation through it with stop reason
`budget_reached`, also when that request used the last permitted turn. A
conversation reset returned with that response is not applied.

With a budget set, a turn that reports neither `usage` nor prompt token
IDs, which the messages trace allows, raises `RolloutContractError`
instead of charging nothing.

Every `TaskSessionSpec` construction must now pass `max_total_tokens`.
In this repository that is only `rolloutengine.test_support`; external
callers such as the SkyRL integration must add it.

---------

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <ravwojdyla@gmail.com>

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Add a messages trace mode for untrained rollouts (#10142)

The turn loop always enforced the exact-token contract, so a model
behind a chat endpoint had to fake token IDs to drive a rollout that
nobody trains on. Chat endpoints re-tokenize the conversation for every
request, so the contract cannot hold there: on GLM-5.3 behind the Orion
router, 2 of 7 recorded 7-turn ShellSim rollouts aborted on a single
non-canonical sampled token in prefixes of 7,000 to 9,700 tokens, and
the router exposes no tokens-in or tokenize route.

`TaskSessionSpec.trace` selects `TraceMode.EXACT_TOKENS`, the default
and the current behavior, or `TraceMode.MESSAGES`. In messages mode the
engine skips the prefix, evidence, logprob and credit checks and keeps
the token IDs a model reports without checking them: the first prompt,
and the last served sequence after it, which is informational only. The
loss mask is all zeros with one value per response token, so the
mask-length invariant still holds, and logprobs are `None`. A model that
reports no token IDs leaves the token fields empty. Every messages
record, including empty and interrupted ones, carries `metrics["trace"]
= "messages"`, so a trainer can refuse it. Token bookkeeping moves out
of the turn loop into one trace class per mode. The engine keeps the
token replay check, which a session triggers by pinning prompt tokens,
and applies it in both modes: a chat endpoint cannot serve pinned
tokens, so a messages rollout whose session pins them now raises instead
of silently running on a different prompt. Under messages mode, the
token counts in `ModelTurnCompleted` events are the unchecked counts the
model reported.

These semantics follow the text token contract in #9781, set per attempt
in `TaskSessionSpec` rather than on the engine, and without requiring
the model to report token IDs.

Fixes #9778

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <ravwojdyla@gmail.com>

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Serve host tool providers in the built-in session (#10141)

Lowering refused every task that declared environment tool providers, so
each new tool set needed its own registered TaskSession. RolloutEngine
now accepts ToolProviders keyed by
`ProviderRequirement.action_interface`. When the shellbox session
prepares, it opens one ToolProviderSession per requirement with a
ToolContext that holds the task machine and the requirement, so each
attempt keeps its own provider state, typically started from
`initial_state`; the sessions close with the attempt's other resources.

The shellbox session serves its shell tool through the same
ToolProviderSession interface, running commands on the task machine, and
dispatches every tool call by name. Shell and provider calls therefore
share one path, including the `ToolCallCompleted` event, and a call that
names no advertised tool returns an unknown-tool error. A ToolCallResult
with `done=True` ends the rollout after that call. Its content is the
observation text, as in a chat tool message. The type is not
taskcompendium's ToolResult, which is a conversation event with a call
id and no `done`.

Lowering still rejects an unregistered interface before machine
acquisition, and now also rejects provider tool names that collide with
the shell, final, answer, or other provider tools. No provider is
registered by default, so existing tasks keep their current behavior.
The docs add a table of the engine's three registries: machine
factories, sessions, and providers.

lower_task and validate_lowered_task take a required providers= keyword,
like sessions=. No caller outside lib/rolloutengine in this repository
uses them; external callers such as the SkyRL integration must pass
providers={}.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[shellbox] Interrupt timed-out ShellSim actions (#10159)

Use Shellsim 0.1.38 cancellation tokens to stop timed-out and cancelled actions. Command deadlines return `TIMED_OUT`; a machine whose worker stops remains available for later commands and file transfers.

Make `ShellSession.interrupt()` stop the active shell action, and cancel active work during shutdown. Block later commands and file transfers during cleanup, with a five-second grace period that repeated cancellation cannot extend. If the worker does not stop, close the machine and reject further operations while it finishes in the background. Log cleanup failures without replacing the caller's cancellation.

Related to #10109. The runtime support is in [Shellsim 0.1.38](https://github.com/rjpower/shellsim/releases/tag/v0.1.38).

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[marina] Release every application independently through Postgres

Release every Marina application from versioned packages in Postgres. Echo, EvalDash, TaskTrove and Zephyr retain their named URLs and existing schemas. Remove the unused Plantt source application and its bootstrap requirement. HTTP routes, MCP tools, agent configuration and scheduled jobs follow the selected package revision. A Marina rollout or restart changes the base runtime without publishing applications or changing their selected revisions.

All applications use `marina release` and one `applet.toml` for package metadata, an optional stable UUID and shared source input paths. Maintained releases default to clean current main and record app and shared build-input hashes. An explicit `--allow-dirty` permits branch or uncommitted source without verified Git provenance; `--local` provides a disposable preview. All updates require an expected revision and publisher/operator authorization. Schema migrations and revision selection share a transaction. Runner capacity and per-application capabilities stay in infrastructure configuration, while jobs execute snapshots of released modules. Child processes retain Marina's working directory so shared libraries can resolve runtime configuration. Python plugins still share runtime dependencies, process resources and service identity.

Remove application source, frontend bundles and filesystem discovery from the production image. The first rollout requires an explicit operator bootstrap of the four named applications. A registry gate precedes both web and scheduled-worker updates, leaving the previous runtime in place until registration succeeds. The [handover runbook](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/infra/marina/README.md#base-runtime-deployment-and-first-cutover) describes the loopback bootstrap and recovery procedure. Before bootstrap, arrange service-account impersonation, choose verified publisher/operator IDs, inspect schema ownership and drain the old scheduled workers. The existing UUID applets Atlas and Filer retain their current UUIDs and selections; dataset loading remains separate from code release. Runtime downgrades must support the active package APIs and dependencies.

[Cutover job incident and recovery](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/766).

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Return run outputs in RolloutData and pass them to TaskSession.grade (#10140)

The engine captured TaskSpec.output_paths only inside sandbox grading
and discarded the files after the grade, so an agent whose job is to
produce a file could not return it to the caller.

The engine now captures the declared outputs once after the turn loop,
inside the verifier deadline and before the session grades, for every
grader kind including SessionGrader. RolloutData.outputs carries the
files. The engine passes the capture to `TaskSession.grade(messages,
stop_reason=..., outputs=...)`, which hands it to the `TaskGrader`, so
the task grader grades the captured files instead of downloading them
again and sessions that grade themselves see them too. Capture failures
still surface as grade interruptions, and a record interrupted before
capture has no outputs.




The new `outputs` keyword is required, so every `TaskSession` outside
this repository, such as the MarinSkyRL sessions, must add it before
taking this version.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[zephyr] Show individual shard input progress in the dashboard (#10167)

Show best-effort input progress for each running Zephyr shard in the
dashboard grid. Parquet and Vortex use cheap row-range totals; shuffle
reducers use partition counts from mapper metadata. Inputs with unknown
totals show striped tiles and records read. Filters can make progress
understate input consumption.

Readers expose an iterator and an optional row total. One wrapper at the
input operation updates task progress and cumulative file-record
counters; shuffle reads retain their separate counters. Direct lookup
reads inside a mapper do not replace the main input or contribute to
those counters. Carry progress separately from counters through inline
and subprocess runners.

Keep progress separate for concurrent mappers and reject snapshots from
earlier attempts or stages. Add shard-state filtering and an inspector
with row counts, elapsed time, average read rate, heartbeat age, and a
worker-task link. Counts reset per input file; reading 100% of an input
can precede output flushing.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Report rollout progress to an optional observer (#10139)

RolloutEngine accepts an optional RolloutObserver and reports each step
of an attempt to it: start, task machine ready, session prepared, each
model turn (stop reason, token counts, model metadata, duration), each
transition, the final grade, and the end of the attempt with its stop
reason or interrupted operation. Each event carries a run key, the task
id and a payload. `run(lowered, run_key=...)` sets the key and defaults
it to the task id, so callers that run a task more than once can tell
the attempts' events apart. Each payload is a frozen dataclass whose
`type` field holds a `RolloutEventType`, so serialized events keep their
type and observers can dispatch on it. Sessions emit their own events
through a required `TaskSessionContext.events` sink; the shellbox
session reports each tool call with its name, duration, and observation
size.

Before this change nothing about a rollout was visible until `run()`
returned, which leaves long agentic attempts opaque while they run.

The engine never awaits the observer, so telemetry cannot change a
rollout. Each attempt queues its events and one task delivers them in
order. Emitting never blocks, and a full queue (1,024 events) drops new
events. After the attempt releases its machines, the engine delivers the
remaining events within `cleanup_timeout`. An observer exception is
logged and ends delivery for that attempt. `RolloutData.metrics` reports
`observer_dropped_events`, `observer_undelivered_events` and
`observer_error_count` when they are nonzero. Events still queued when
the process dies are lost.

This is one of six independent changes that prepare RolloutEngine for an
agent layer: a prompt, an environment, tools and limits, bound at run
time to a model and a machine backend. A task-generation agent that
wrote and tested TaskSpecs inside a rollout motivated the series. The
others are #10140 (run outputs), #10141 (tool providers), #10142 (trace
modes), #10143 (token budget), #10144 (output spill); most of them edit
the turn loop, so later merges need a rebase.

The events add emit calls to `_run_session`, which was already long;
splitting it is left for a separate change.

---------

Co-authored-by: Rafal Wojdyla <ravwojdyla@gmail.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finestore] Compact bounded writer-owned shards on close (#10168)

Compact each writer’s residual level-zero shards when FineStore closes,
after flushing pending writes. Small archives that finish below the
16-shard maintenance limit can otherwise retain many descriptor files
and amplify every blob lookup.

Merge groups of at least two shards within an input budget of 64 MiB and
16,384 rows across all tables in one close call. Visit blob descriptors
first, then other registered tables in name order, skipping groups that
exceed the remaining budget. Select only the closing writer’s level-zero
inputs so closes with distinct writer IDs use disjoint groups and
repeated sessions preserve earlier compacted data. Reuse the full
manifest as the publication base, retaining concurrent additions and row
commit ordering.

Retry classified transient storage failures with exponential backoff for
up to three attempts per snapshot or merge, then propagate errors after
durable flush. Explicit cache close compacts normally; the cache’s
process-exit handler only requests maintenance shutdown after its
bounded write drain, so further storage I/O cannot hold interpreter
exit.

The pass adds close latency and may repeat input reads and writes on
retry. It does not repair archives left by killed writers or guarantee
one shard across repeated sessions. Explicit compaction, sealing, and
background thresholds retain their existing behavior.

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[taskforge] Add the build step DAG and its memo store (#10081)

Add the author and build stages of Taskforge as `stage30_author` and
`stage40_build`. An author writes async steps decorated with
`@rl_env_build_step`, which takes a step's inputs from its parameters
after the context, and a final step decorated with `@rl_env_build_sink`,
which reads its inputs the same way and refuses any return annotation
other than `TaskSpec`. `rl_env_build_program(*steps, sink=...)` orders
the steps by Kahn's algorithm, breaking ties by declaration order and
running the sink last. It refuses duplicate names, unknown inputs,
cycles, a step taking the sink as an input, and a step whose output
reaches neither another step nor the sink, since that output would never
enter the task. A step receives an `RLEnvBuildContext` (item id, model,
sampling policy) and then its inputs by name, where a parameter called
`proposal` receives the caller's proposal, an opaque JSON value at this
point in the stack. `static_author` hands back a hand-written program as
an author. `run_program` returns the sink's `TaskSpec`, and `run_build`
writes it to `draft/task.json` with an `ItemBuildProvenance` in
`draft/provenance.json`, which lists every step's stored memo beside
that build's hit or miss status for it. The status belongs to the build
and stays out of the stored memo, which the store writes only on a miss.

Each step's output is memoized under a key of `SDK_VERSION`, the sha256
of the step's own source, the content digest of each declared input, and
a model digest over the model id and the sampling policy. Because inputs
enter the key by content, a step that reruns with an identical output
leaves its consumers cached. A helper read from outside a step body is
not in the key, so changing one needs a declared input or an
`SDK_VERSION` bump. Item ids belong to the caller and are only checked
for file safety.

The store is a hand-rolled memo of about 60 lines over rigging's
`StoragePath` and `atomic_rename`, holding content-addressed JSON blobs
and per-item memos under a local path or an object-store URL. joblib
keys on function identity and clears a function's whole cache when its
code changes, so it reuses nothing across program revisions, and Marin's
`StepSpec` hashes no code and costs a status file and a distributed lock
per step. Its `load` and `store` take a caller-built key, and `memoized`
is the one call the runner and a driver use, so a driver can memoize a
helper against the same store with a key it builds. `memoized(store,
name, key, output_type, compute)` loads under such a key and on a miss
awaits `compute` and stores the result, and `run_program` calls it for
every step.

Stage packages are numbered by tens in pipeline order (proposal 10,
triage 20, author 30, build 40), and `tests/test_imports.py` fails when
a stage imports a higher-numbered one.

The design comes from draft #9993. Later PRs bring back the proposal
package, the ledger, the author's programs written by the language
model, the validate and review stages, and the stage coordinator.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[zephyr] Batch Vortex file reads (#10153)

Read Vortex files in 65,536-row batches. Previously, a ranged read built
an index for every row in the requested range, and both ranged and
full-file reads materialized a complete Arrow table before yielding
records. The new path limits temporary index arrays and Arrow results to
one batch at a time.

Reader tests cover filtering and projection across a batch boundary,
along with row-range and empty-file behavior.

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[rolloutengine] Name the failed setup command and keep its output in the error (#10129)

When an environment setup command exits non-zero, `_prepare_machine`
raised `Environment setup command failed: exited, exit=1` and nothing
else. In the Taskforge backend A/B on 2026-10-14, two tasks failed every
trial that way on the local backend (their setup wrote under `/opt`,
which that backend mounts read-only), and the attempt records could not
say why; the cause was found by reading the task's `setup_commands` and
the backend's mount list by hand.

The error now names the command and keeps the last 2,000 characters of
its stdout and stderr (`SETUP_OUTPUT_CHARS`), decoded with replacement,
so a failed setup reads as `Environment setup command failed: exited,
exit=1; command: 'mkdir -p /workspace /opt/gen'; stdout: ''; stderr:
"mkdir: cannot create directory '/opt/gen': Read-only file system"`. The
timeout path is unchanged.

A machine-shell test covers a setup command returning exit 1 with output
on both streams and checks that start fails with this message.

---

description](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10129#issuecomment-6179074788)

commits.message:
Register the pinned Skill2Env release in the curation catalog (#10120)

Add Skill2Env's 7,496-task Harbor Hub release to the current curation
inventory. Pin release 1.0.1 by its content digest. Use `Harbor Hub` as
the origin and `Harbor Hub:skill2env` as the stable source ID: the
origin identifies the intake source, following the existing MarinSkyRL
and Task Trove convention. This replaces the generic “Registered
releases” label proposed in #9881. Catalog notes describe the source
format, benchmark distinction, and licensing caveat.

The count comes from exact release membership checked on 2026-10-01. Hub
revision 2 is version 1.0.1, with tags `latest` and `v1.0`; the digest
fixes the release independently of those tags. The unfinished
investigation in #9630 confirmed a verifier defect in one sampled task.
That remains an unresolved caveat for follow-up validation, not a
completed dataset assessment.

The source has no conversion pipeline, so catalog publication records it
as unassessed with “No conversion pipeline.” Downloading, conversion,
and automatic assessment belong in a follow-up. The entry becomes
visible after catalog publication and Atlas reload; this PR does not
publish either.

Part of #9630

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[rl] Support separate reference roles and remote artifact steps (#10113)

SkyRL role planning on current main cannot express a separate reference
footprint: colocation is hardcoded, capacity accounting ignores
reference GPUs, backend YAML checks duplicate topology concerns, and a
Megatron forward/train microbatch mismatch allocates GPUs before
failing. This promotes policy/reference colocation to validated topology
fields with footprint and capacity checks, removes the superseded YAML
checks, rejects microbatch mismatch before submission, and updates every
role-plan call site plus the SkyRL lock so the isolated launcher
resolves on all platforms.

Remote artifact steps are broken in the lazy framework: a RemoteCallable
is not directly callable for local runs, the lowered spec drops remote
metadata, and Iris submissions double-write the step record. This
unwraps the callable for local execution, preserves remote-ness in the
spec, and skips the redundant record write on the submit path.

The RL coordinator also lacks the dedicated Daytona keys, so rollout and
eval workloads cannot use separate credentials. This forwards
DAYTONA_RL_API_KEY and DAYTONA_EVAL_API_KEY alongside the existing key.

One known gap: the Iris double-write guard has no direct test yet.

Part of #10040.

---------

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[levanter] Exclude cache markers from Hugging Face mirrors (#10039)

Skip a Hugging Face repository file when its name matches the configured
cache completion marker. The DARE-TIES-02 repository contains
`.cache_metadata.json` from its Base cache. During streaming, that file
reached the regional mirror before all weight shards. A follower then
logged a cache hit on a 90 GB mirror containing only 28 of 39 shards.

The regression test interrupts a weight download and verifies that the
marker remains absent until a successful retry. Existing partial mirrors
with a copied marker need separate cleanup.

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Count sliding-window attention in base MoE MFU (#7934)

Count sliding-window attention when reporting model FLOP utilization
(MFU) for the base MoE template. The previous calculation treated every
layer as full attention and overstated MFU when the window was shorter
than the sequence.

Use the same layer schedule for the forward pass and the FLOP estimate.
Every fourth layer and the final layer use full attention. All other
layers use the configured sliding window. Pass the full-attention layer
count explicitly to include the final layer when the total depth is not
divisible by four.

The compute-budget heuristic retains its full-attention convention
because its learning-rate and batch-size fits use that convention. This
change corrects reported FLOPs without changing training configurations
or model outputs.
